title: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment.…
content: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. Udāyi, I say: ‘This person is not bound, not fettered.’ Why is that? Udāyi, the difference in his faculties has been fully understood by me.”

title: Elder Nun Mother of Abhayā: From the soles of the feet upward, From the top of the head downward — Contemplate this body — This…
content:
Elder Nun Mother of Abhayā:

From the soles of the feet upward,
From the top of the head downward —
Contemplate this body —
This body is truly impure,
Truly foul, stinking.

Thus abiding,
All sensual desire is uprooted.
Fever is abandoned —
I am cooled, at peace.

title: “Monks, here a monk, reflecting wisely, does not consent to arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to…
content: “Monks, here a monk, reflecting wisely, does not consent to arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to arisen ill-will thought … does not consent to arisen harmful thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to any arisen evil, unwholesome states; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes them non-existent.”

title: “And how, good sirs, is one defiled by sensual lust? Here, good sirs, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached…
content: “And how, good sirs, is one defiled by sensual lust? Here, good sirs, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. When he tastes a flavor with the tongue … When he cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, he is attached to agreeable phenomena and repelled by disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. This, good sirs, is called a monk who is defiled by sensual lust regarding forms cognizable by the eye … regarding tastes … regarding phenomena cognizable by the mind. A monk living thus, good sirs, if Māra approaches him through the eye, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object. If Māra approaches him through the tongue … through the mind, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object.”

title: Elder Talapuṭa: O mind, everywhere, I have acted as you wished, For many lives — You were not angry with me, And this inner-born body…
content:
Elder Talapuṭa:

O mind, everywhere,
I have acted as you wished,
For many lives —
You were not angry with me,
And this inner-born body
Is your gratitude!
On the long path of saṃsāra,
Suffering was caused by you.

O mind, you yourself made
This person that I am —
You made me become
A brahmin,
A king, a royal,
One day a merchant,
Another day a servant,
Or a kind of deity —
All is due to you,
Made by you.

Due to your power,
We became asuras —
Due to you,
I fell to the bottom of hell;
Sometimes an animal,
Sometimes a hungry ghost —
All is due to you,
Made by you.

You will not deceive me
Again, many times more,
Like sorcerers
Performing magic tricks.
You played tricks on me,
Like playing with a madman.
O mind, tell me —
Where have I wronged you?

Formerly this mind wandered,
Went wherever it wished,
Went where it delighted,
Went where it enjoyed —
Now I will restrain it
With wise reflection,
As with a hook one restrains
A rutting elephant.

For me, the Teacher
Has declared that life is impermanent —
Life is not eternal,
Life has no core.
O mind, urge me
To leap into the Buddha’s teaching —
Make me cross the flood,
So very hard to cross.

I have now gone forth
In the Great Sage’s Dhamma —
Those like me
Do not accept loss.

Forests, oceans, rivers, land,
The four directions, above and below —
All are impermanent.
The three realms are perilous.
O mind, where will you go?
You will enjoy peace.

title: “‘Visible here and now, visible here and now (sanditthiko),’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Dhamma visible here and now,…
content: “‘Visible here and now, visible here and now (sanditthiko),’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Here, Upavāna, having seen a form with the eye, a monk experiences the form but does not experience lust for the form, and there is no inner lust for forms. He knows: ‘There is no inner lust for forms in me.’ As long as, Upavāna, having seen a form with the eye, a monk experiences the form but does not experience lust for the form, and there is no inner lust for forms — he knows that — thus, Upavāna, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

title: (The Blessed One): I am freed From Māra’s trap, Freed from the bonds of sensual pleasures, Both heavenly and human. I am freed From Māra’s…
content:
(The Blessed One):
I am freed
From Māra’s trap,
Freed from the bonds of sensual pleasures,
Both heavenly and human.
I am freed
From Māra’s fetter.
O Death, you are
Defeated.

title: “And what, Aggivessana, is trained body and trained mind? Here, Aggivessana, a well-taught noble disciple experiences a pleasant feeling. Having felt that pleasant feeling, he…
content: “And what, Aggivessana, is trained body and trained mind? Here, Aggivessana, a well-taught noble disciple experiences a pleasant feeling. Having felt that pleasant feeling, he does not lust after it, does not fall into lust for pleasure. If that pleasant feeling ceases, and due to its cessation, a painful feeling arises, he does not sorrow, grieve, lament, beat his breast, or become distraught. Aggivessana, that pleasant feeling arises for him but does not invade his mind and remain because the body is trained. That painful feeling arises for him but does not invade his mind and remain because the mind is trained. In this manner, for a person in whom either way — pleasant feeling arises and does not invade his mind because the body is trained, and painful feeling arises and does not invade his mind because the mind is trained — he is one with trained body and trained mind.”

title: Seclusion is happiness For one who knows contentment, For one who has heard the Dhamma, For one who sees rightly. Non-ill-will is happiness For those…
content:
Seclusion is happiness
For one who knows contentment,
For one who has heard the Dhamma,
For one who sees rightly.

Non-ill-will is happiness
For those in the world
Who practice self-restraint
Toward living beings.

Dispassion is happiness
For those who transcend sensual pleasures,
Who subdue the conceit ‘I am’ —
This is the highest happiness.

title: “Monks, an untaught ordinary person does not know as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard…
content: “Monks, an untaught ordinary person does not know as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Monks, a well-taught noble disciple knows as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.”
